idiom_name: Ktor Sessions plugin (cookie or header transport, pluggable SessionStorage)
implementation_notes: The Sessions plugin replaces the classic manager: install(Sessions) { cookie<UserSession>(...) } registers a typed session, call.sessions.set/get/clear are the life-cycle calls, and SessionStorage (SessionStorageMemory, directorySessionStorage or a custom implementation with read/write/invalidate(id)) decides whether the payload stays server-side or travels to the client. Client-side payloads must be wrapped in SessionTransportTransformerEncrypt (AES plus HMAC-SHA256 by default); server-side payloads send only an identifier. Policy calls remain: clear on logout, issue a fresh session after authentication, and configure maxAgeInSeconds, path and SameSite.
pitfalls: A cookie session without transform(...) puts the payload in a client-readable cookie; Ktor signs and encrypts only when configured to.
SessionStorageMemory is per-process and disappears on restart; multi-instance deployments need directory, Redis or database storage behind the SessionStorage interface.
Sessions are read on every request unless the io.ktor.server.sessions.deferred system property is enabled, so custom storage sees a read per request even when the handler never touches the session.
